analysis:
This PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (a new load-time shape-warmup section at head lines ~980-1027, plus unchanged surrounding text in the supplied units) and a new DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP row in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1745). I examined the supplied head text for the inference.md units (lines 1631-2460) and the cli-reference patch. The 980-1027 section itself is only visible as a truncated patch excerpt, and its source (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift) is not supplied, so I could not verify the warmup behavior.

Security-relevant observations, with no regression found:
- The warmup runs synthetic greedy probes and cells that are excluded from rate and counter training (per the doc). It uses the artifact's default sampling and a 20 s wall budget. It does not touch consumer prompts (A-001), keys (A-003), or attestation and authorization (TB-011).
- Possible interaction with the prefix cache (T-041): the warmup prompts are synthetic. If they donate to the SSD prefix cache, they could add at-rest artifacts or perturb the cache epoch and routing evidence. Whether warmup requests carry a cacheSalt, are non-cacheable, or cannot donate is not shown in the supplied evidence. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.
- The new env var DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP (0 disables; 'always' skips the shader-cache probe) is a local operator knob. It is documented as a tuning control only and grants no trust or authorization.
- The remaining text (tool parsing, reasoning seeds, MiMo media memory accounting, Flint constraints) is descriptive of existing behavior. Any claims about stricter memory, size, or schema bounds are documentation, not changed code, and cannot be verified here.

For the next pass: confirm the warmup path in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift and EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibration.swift neither donates to SSD prefix cache nor exposes synthetic prompt content in logs or telemetry, and does not perturb the cache epoch or routing evidence.
